- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.2) and forecast is flat or rising, aggressively lower forecast to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- When true outcome shows sharp downward spike after a peak, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next period.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome over 5+ days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.0x the average deviation from recent 7-day mean.  
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period and forecast continues upward, cut forecast slope by 20–30% to avoid lagged overreaction.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust forecast downward by 2–3% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +0.2 to -0.3), forecast should be smoother — dampen trend magnitude by 15–25%.
